polls.text: Do you feel strongly that we should keep the 'synthetic' term in the draft?

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Hey, Mark!

chat.author: Timid Zehta
chat.text: greetings

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: @Kevin very good, though I think I overdid it a bit with the running the day after

chat.author: Mark Nottingham
chat.text: (we'l wait for another minute or two, for those who missed my message)

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: @Paul oh no!  safe trip home, though?

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: Good 4 am morning! :skull_and_crossbones:

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: https://github.com/ietf-wg-aipref/drafts/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+label%3Avocabulary

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: 4am, ouch

chat.author: Suresh Krishnan
chat.text: Are you traveling Farz? Sorry about the timing.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: yeah ... it's ok. we can't accommodate to my travel schedule... Ill go do yoga after this and be fresh.

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Cool!

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: yeah, the first issue will be answered by that PR

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Oh, sorry.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: do we have consensus on any part?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: close

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: I think Mark was saying "at some point we need to start the formal consensus proccess".

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Not to put words in his mouth.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: the chairs haven't really declared consensus on anything; I heard that they would like to find points on which they can declare

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: :clap:

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: https://github.com/ietf-wg-aipref/drafts/issues/153 and https://github.com/ietf-wg-aipref/drafts/issues/154 are still deferred, so it's not urgent to answer those

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: we can solve this when we solved everything else

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Any noun will do

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: this is a one on one word substitution

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: sorry which issues are those?

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: we can just call it Bavarian grarmet

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: we should call it the flying persian rug!

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: @farz #163

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: so instead of assets we say artifacts?

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: no "persian flying carpet"

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: That's the idea here Farz.

chat.author: Timid Zehta
chat.text: i'm mostly ambivalent if the term used is defined

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Timid Robot, I failed to do a case-insensitive search and replace  :face_palm:

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: great. I kind of like it better than assets

chat.author: Eric Rescorla
chat.text: assefacts

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Happy to tighten this up, sure

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: +1 to what EKR said

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: what do you think about that, chris?

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: that's exactly right, yes

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: does the phrase "generate content" not address that line between classifiers and generators

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: It arguably could, Martin, but the idea is not to ensure that we save every byte we can but to be evocative of the thing we're trying to describe.

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: (I think)

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: But ekr's point is solid.  We've added text to address the classification/ranking/scoring thing.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: I think someone also mentioned that sometimes classifiers do generate content.

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: I'm not sure that I feel particularly strongly about keeping it, but I don't see any point in removing it, either.

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: Farz -- see "even where the model generates rationale for its output"

chat.author: Suresh Krishnan
chat.text: @Farz, that is the rationale text

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: I just don't see it changing the meaning at all.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Warren pointed out that you can turn any classifier into a generator, sure.  (That's largely a theoretical point though.)

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: oh yes good good. I am not imagining things

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Mark, we did that

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: The discussion 2x ago referred to the dictionary, which has a very good definition for the term.

chat.author: Mark Nottingham
chat.text: I meant in-document, as we do elsewhere

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: We could just say "LLM", but Alissa didn't like "large"...

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: The point was that the dictionary meaning suffices: 1. Relating to, involving, or of the nature of synthesis. 2. Produced by synthesis, especially not of natural origin. 3. Prepared or made artificially.

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: And I think "prepared or made" might address Chris Needham's concern, no?

chat.author: Eric Rescorla
chat.text:
Kevin Kelley said:

We could just say "LLM", but Alissa didn't like "large"...

L?LM

chat.author: Mark Nottingham
chat.text: but that begs the question -- what is the state of nature here?

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: well it goes both ways

chat.author: Timid Zehta
chat.text: my weak preference to keep "synthetic" has changed to a weak preference to remove it

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: such is the nature of weak preferences :)

chat.author: Eric Rescorla
chat.text: I'm not invested, but I think if we're proposing a text change now, we should do a hum to see what people think rather than continue to discuss in detail

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: I havent heard a strong argument to remove it.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: There are no strong arguments either way here.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: yeah

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: we are stuck

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Per Martin, the dictionary definition!

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: yes dictionary def is ok ..

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: Martin can we do this during IETF

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: This is a great opportunity to test how people think.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: That might not resolve the issue finally, but this is the core crowd.  I'd rather spend IETF meeting time on more substantive issues.

chat.author: Brendan Quinn
chat.text: From my point of view I think "used to generate" is basically a synonym of "synthetic", so "An AI model that is used toi generate content in one or more modalities" is fine by me. Any time we at IPTC have used "synthetic" it's because we didn't use the word "generate" or "generative", our vocabularies were first published in 2022 before the word "generative" become common parlance, so please don't assume that we are in favour just because we use the word. I would prefer not to defer it and just to go ahead and make changes. We need to press forward.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: fine

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Naturally, if you say "yes", you are then obligated to help motivate its retention.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: it goes both ways

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: In this case, the argument I've heard is that it is at best redundant.  If it is redundant or ambiguous, that's motivation enough to remove it.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: that is your assessment Martin. I don't agree.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: I saw the poll as sufficient motivation to remove on that basis.  I welcome the introduction of a counter argument in favour of retention.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: people didnt know there was going to be substantive discussion and polling during this meeting. I don't see a fully fledged agenda.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: This is pretty clear, I think.  The reason we have the issue is because some people might prefer removing it.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: The scraping issue is addressed by #253 ekr.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: oh is this the flying sticky preference?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text:
#252 adds "Where acquisition and use of assets occur at different times
or in different parts of systems,
retaining any usage preferences associated with those assets
ensures that they are available to inform decisions about use."
#252 adds "Retaining preferences with assets that are transformed
into an alternative format prior to their use,
including the creation of embeddings or other simplified forms,
also provides an opportunity to apply preferences
at the point of use."

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: I don't like the word compliance. is that the word we use througought?

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: my hand has been down for a while!

chat.author: Eric Rescorla
chat.text: I suggest we revisit this once people have had an oppty to read #253

chat.author: Brendan Quinn
chat.text: AFAICR the EU AI Act code of practice, for example places requirements on people who are crawling but not training... so there is precedent

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: Many issues were raised  with embedding and traveling preferences.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: well I don't know if we can really say it's not onerous for everyone... (replying to Timid, sorry I am slow today)

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Did Mark just disappear, or is it me?

chat.author: Mark Nottingham
chat.text: audio issues

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: no it's for me too

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Yes!

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: yeah

chat.author: Timid Zehta
chat.text: you're back!

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: "transformed to an alternative format" is pretty generic; that would include tokenization (embeddings are downstream of tokenization generally)

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: sorry transformed from what to what

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: from how it was obtained to anything else

chat.author: Sebastian Posth
chat.text:
We distinguish between parties that access content and parties that use the content.
Is this an issue when the party crawling but not using the content does not provide the preferences? 
This means that the preferences would apply to the parties who are not using it.

chat.author: Krishna Madhavan
chat.text: I think there is a conflation of concepts going on here. I do not really see how this helps or what changes in practice.

chat.author: Suresh Krishnan
chat.text: @Krishna, can you elaborate?

chat.author: Krishna Madhavan
chat.text: There is profound differences between how data for model training is distriubted vs. how they are used in various experiences

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Okay, thanks Nate!  I'm not sure either; it was just a thought.

chat.author: Brendan Quinn
chat.text: it may be about embeddings today, it could be another technology tomorrow, so I think we need to say that preferences must travel with the content in a generic way. Otherwise it just becomes a loophole that people can exploit in the future. Businesses may emerge that take data, manipulate it in some way that evades our definition, and sell/pass it on. So the more generic the statement, the better.

chat.author: Sebastian Posth
chat.text: I would add "different parties". But that still means that preferences apply when parties do not use the content.

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: I think Brendan has captured the concern well

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: To make a record, I (and many artists) want to express a preference as to all input to gen AI models

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: I know!  That's why I threw in the last few lines :)

chat.author: Alissa Cooper
chat.text: audio not working sorry

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: Ok. But for me, I'd want to delete everything after the comma. Or else have a separate category that is expressible.

chat.author: Sebastian Posth
chat.text: What does "interact" mean? – Summarize, translate, modify?

chat.author: Eric Rescorla
chat.text: AI-usage-1

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Ah, yes, I should have mentioned---Chris and I deliberately didn't spend any time on the name.

chat.author: Brendan Quinn
chat.text: +1 to timid's point about giving this a more specific name - it doesn't make sense to effectively say "ai-use means AI use except for one particular kind of AI use". When reduced like that, it seems a bit nonsensical

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Re: Brad: but then we wound up in the discussion about uploading a file vs. pasting a URL.

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: sorry when was this suggested?

chat.author: Bradley Silver
chat.text: Also, "intent" is to be established how?

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: so this entangles the user ...

chat.author: Brendan Quinn
chat.text: Alissa's example said "BBC homepage" which does actually identify one specific asset...

chat.author: Eric Rescorla
chat.text: Is the "specific/general" distinction whether an AI system is needed to dereference whatever the user has asked the system to do or whether it can be done by deterministic non-AI mechanisms

chat.author: Elaine Newton
chat.text: *where the user expressed intent?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Kevin is there a line between "https://bbc.co.uk" and "bbc.co.uk"?  I can understand how there might be a line between "bbc.co.uk" and "the BBC homepage".  Just trying to be clear.

chat.author: Bradley Silver
chat.text: Has visibility is not clear.    Has access to?  Has accessed?

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: I think "go walk the whole domain and analyze the data for me in some way" is something we intended to be covered by this definition.

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: And just in case this wasn't clear, these are NOT fully-baked thoughts! Input very welcome.

chat.author: Sebastian Posth
chat.text: So the user has to download the content from the website first to create an artefact before providing it directly to the system? I do not understand the difference between asset (online) and asset (local).

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: we need an accessibility carve-out. what happened to that conversation? because this stuff is going to have an impact on accessibility and libraries universities have repeatedly said it

chat.author: Bradley Silver
chat.text: Sebastian the difference would be whether the user ever visits the page/site, or not.  If the exclusion means the preference does not cover instances where the user says, summarize the article in this publication at this location, and never visits the site, then surely the publisher has an interest in expressing a preference about that?

chat.author: Kevin Kelley
chat.text: Well, Chris, it sounds like we have some work to do ;)

chat.author: Paul Keller
chat.text: but is that something a preference can solve?

chat.author: Alissa Cooper
chat.text: I offered the exception idea because I’m not sure the position Nate is expressing will have consensus here for the purposes of this vocab and it’s eventual use in REP

chat.author: Alissa Cooper
chat.text: *its

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: we are not supposed to characterize consensus is my understanding

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: becuase it kinda makes it hard for me to get consensus for my points!

chat.author: Alissa Cooper
chat.text: I don’t know what that means

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: I need an opportunity to get consensus. By saying we won't consider something without consensus, I can't do that. I think the IETF says we shouldn't characterize consensus for this reason

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Having a user-directed exclusion might make a11y exclusions less necessary, but I'd encourage people to try to find language we can use to specifically exclude a11y here.

chat.author: Alissa Cooper
chat.text: Well we’ve all had years of opportunity at this point

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: absolutely

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: Meredith has mentioned many examples

chat.author: Farzaneh
chat.text: AI is pretty human ;) unfortunately trained on human content with all its bad and good things.

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: engage with the wiki use cases!

chat.author: Nate Hake
chat.text: or stop telling me to bury my concerns there please
